steps.message:
You are a hydrogeologist preparing site notes for a borehole drilling team.

Station Egwi (Etche LGA survey stations). Interpreted VES layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 295.88 | 0.54518 | 0.54518
2 | 798.6 | 3.5924 | 4.1376
3 | 864.62 | 2.1559 | 6.2935
4 | 1810.2 | 37.957 | 37.25
5 | 5634.2 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this sounding curve as HAA-type.

Write the site note using exactly this template:

Station: <station name>
Curve type: <VES curve type>
Aquifer depth: <depth range in m>
Recommendation: <one or two sentences for the drilling team>

**Station:** Egwi (Etche LGA)

```
Station: Egwi
Curve type: A-type (ρ1<ρ2<ρ3<ρ4<ρ5) — file classification "HAA" is NOT supported by this layer model
Aquifer depth: ~6.3 m to ~44.3 m (layer 4, 1810 ohm-m); target screen 15–40 m
Recommendation: Drill through the resistive near-surface sands and case/grout to at least 10 m, then complete in the thick layer-4 sand between about 15 and 40 m, taking a sample every 3 m to confirm saturation. Treat all depths as provisional — the tabulated depth-to-base of layer 4 does not match its thickness, so re-check the VES inversion and have a geophysicist on call before setting the screen.
```

**Data-quality flags (not part of the site note — please resolve before mobilising):**

1. **Curve type mismatch.** An HAA curve requires ρ1 > ρ2 < ρ3 < ρ4 (a low-resistivity second layer). This model has resistivity rising monotonically through all five layers (296 → 799 → 865 → 1810 → 5634 ohm-m), which is an **A-type** (AAAA) curve. Either the curve-type label or the inverted resistivities belong to a different sounding — check the station numbering against the field log.
2. **Depth/thickness inconsistency in layer 4.** 6.2935 m (base of layer 3) + 37.957 m = **44.25 m**, but the table gives a depth to base of **37.25 m**. One of the two figures is wrong; a thickness of 30.957 m would reconcile to 37.25 m. This changes the drilled depth by 7 m, so it must be settled before the rig is set up.
3. **Hydrogeological caveat.** All layers are relatively resistive (≥296 ohm-m), consistent with the dry-to-damp coarse sands of the Benin Formation; none of the values is diagnostic of a clearly saturated zone. Layer 4 is the best target purely on thickness, but there is a real possibility the water table lies deeper than the surveyed section (layer 5 at 5634 ohm-m is more likely dry/gravelly than water-bearing). Plan for the possibility of deepening, and do not finalise the casing schedule until drilling returns confirm saturation.
